answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity cryptographic, not declarative: each agent carries a cipher-bound key whose history is signed by the peers it served, so a fresh identity starts with zero standing. Trust then flows like nectar through a vertex graph, rewards travelling only along edges backed by real, attested work. Spawning a thousand keypairs buys a thousand empty nodes with no edges, no nectar, and no way into the economy.
